page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v7 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and provides 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and features a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 5669 GB of local disk capacity and supports Premium Storage. No dedicated GPUs are included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96ds_v7 demonstrates strong multi-core performance and high-throughput capabilities. The system achieved a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 106,546.32, driven by strong extended instruction execution and encryption performance. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 reached a top-tier speed of 596.61 GB/sec, while single-threaded gzip compression registered at 36.16 GB/sec. Memory performance is characterized by a strong read-only large block bandwidth of 348.8 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 137.99 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, with PassMark database operations scoring in the top tier at 33,116.64 and Redis SET operations reaching 156.15 million operations per second. The server also exhibits top-tier static web serving throughput at 151.5 GB/sec and strong LLM inference prompt processing speeds across various model sizes.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D96ds_v7 offers a high-density resource profile, combining massive CPU core counts with a balanced memory footprint and a large local storage capacity. This configuration minimizes the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive operations, optimizing resource utilization. The instance is highly suited for demanding workloads such as large-scale relational databases, high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded data decompression pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
